quotes.text: When a stranger's record shines, give fully. Trust that is held back halfway earns only half a harvest.
On it, every giver and every returner left a mark, so that each stranger arrived already known.
So the hills carved their fifth law
In the seventh season of Sefa's winds
The wise towns learned to judge hearts across many seasons, not by a single wind.
Whoever carries the risk should walk home a little richer.
"Your last partner was stingy," she said, "but I am not them.
"Only four crossed. Perhaps he held one back. Pay him for four and no more."
"What if he remembers only the thin count? What if he takes revenge now?"

note: Crossroads stone of marks; ten numbered laws of Sefa's winds; Kael declines to punish Mira for a past partner's stinginess.

quotes.text: When courage crosses the water, answer with a little more than fairness.
Across the water waited a stranger whose marks were carved in the reeds.
Beneath Tamsin's words she carved a sixth line
If I punish the mist, I punish the faithful.
"And if they choose poorly?" asked Keth.
Should my answer be smaller than their courage?
"No one watches this shore. Keep them all."
What if the stranger changes?

note: Tamsin then Lirien; reed marks as record; brother's hoarding suggestions refused; one carved line per season.

quotes.text: Trust a little with a stranger, and trust fully with a proven heart.
Yet every stone on the bridge held the echo of every gift ever given.
They carved the sixth law
In the seventh season of the bridge over the River Vael
A whisper rose from the reeds: "The rope is strong now. One frayed strand will not break it."
Each assumed kindness had been lost in the mist, not withheld.
The fog tempted her. *Who would know?* But the bridge carried echoes
Orrin carried the risk, so Orrin should carry home the larger share.
"Will you give everything again?"
What if her gift is lost in the gray?
*Give first, return fairly, and forgive the fog.*

note: Dessa on the bridge of Vael; echo-stones, mirrors, knotted rope; reeds' whispers to cheat rejected; numbered laws.

quotes.text: Those who keep pouring through lean seasons deserve the fullest returns.
Every pouring and every returning left a groove in the stone, and rain filled the grooves so that all could read them.
Kael carved the fifth law of Oma
In the sixth age of Oma
If you hold back because of fog, you punish Vesh for what the mountain did.
so that Mira, who had risked the most, drank the most.
Return as if you will be seen.
"Why do the faithful keep pouring when their returns come back thin?"
A law carved only for others is no law at all.

note: Ages of Oma; grooves record deeds; tenth law 'Keep the laws you carve'; bold pourer never punished.

quotes.text: Where doubt clouds the water, let generosity clear it.
"A stranger is only someone whose deeds you have not yet read," Isen said.
In the eighth season of Amareth, Veyla turned the wheel
I will not punish a friend for the fog's hunger.
The one who casts carries the risk, and the one who receives must honor it.
No ferryman stood watching.
The young ones asked, "What if she keeps them all?"
"Will he think you cheated him? Will he hold back now?"
trust the stranger first, repay beyond fairness

note: Isen and the riverstones of Amareth; returns half plus a fog margin; young ones' 'return him less' refused.

quotes.text: "Then the reeds would show it," Joru answered, "and the next shore would guard itself.
Whoever hoards is soon met with empty rafts.
To those who have proven true, give everything.
The keeper pointed to the reeds, where every crossing left a mark: who had given, who had returned, who had hoarded.
In the third season of the delta
One fogged crossing is noise, but a hundred crossings are a heart.
"But no one forced them," Anwe said. "A receiver could keep the whole raft."
"What if she had kept it all?"
*Give first, but give with sense.
so the one who had carried the risk would walk home with more than they began with and more than she kept.

note: Delta reeds record hoarders, who meet empty rafts; Anwe becomes keeper; apprentice's hold-back suggestions answered.

quotes.text: Soon Sela noticed that the eastern gifts were drifting past her shore. They were going to kinder banks
this time he watched closely to see who honored his faith.
Her storehouse, once overflowing, slowly emptied.
When the fog thins your answer, thicken the next one.
Ferrymen poled from bank to bank, telling who had divided fairly and who had hoarded, so no gift traveled blind.
The bold giver deserves the fullest share.
He had learned that one thin return is only weather. A lifetime of thin returns would be a choice
*No one would know,* he thought.
"Why give extra when they gave less?" his sister asked.
"And if they keep it all?" his sister asked.

note: Greedy Sela kept ten of fifteen; gifts drift past her shore until she repents; later Lirien's line carved (from A2).

quotes.text: Those who hoard are remembered too, and soon find no baskets drifting toward them.
The elders say the river keeps a memory of every crossing.
When the giver holds nothing back, the receiver must hold nothing false.
The elders say the river keeps a memory of every crossing.
The elders carved the eighth law
In the ninth season the river set Toren on the eastern bank again.
"No one would see if I kept every basket."
If I punish the stranger for what the river blurs, I teach them to doubt
"Will you not keep one basket, in case the river turns cruel?"
"And if the fog returns less than you hoped?" the fisher asked.
*Give first, but give with sense.

note: Toren across ten seasons; quotes Oru and Tamsa's law from A6; hoarders remembered and shunned; grandson's hold-back advice refused.

phrase: Give first, but give with sense. Return more than you owe. Forgive the fog.
note: Also 'Whoever receives must remember the fear of giving' (A8 R4, A2 R6); 'Receive as you would wish to be received' (A7, A6); A7 cites Lirien's line.
